finance.subtitle: Money by the day: what each department costs, what comes in, and loans from friends abroad.

tiles.treasuryNote: Kept above half a month of spending by automatic borrowing.
tiles.perDayNote: This month's balance over its {{days}} days, before borrowing.
tiles.loansNote: All loans together are capped at {{ceiling}}.
tiles.marketNote: What automatic borrowing costs. Average on the debt: {{average}}.

finance.expensesNote: Each department's cost per day this month: its allocation plus the upkeep of what it runs.
finance.loansNote: Countries lend to India when there is an embassy and relations are warm; the international lender looks at India's reputation. Every lender undercuts the market rate that automatic borrowing pays. A loan is repaid in full when it falls due; a missed repayment rolls into debt and costs reputation and the lender's goodwill.
finance.terms: Rate {{rate}} a year: {{interest}} a month in interest. This lender lends up to {{cap}}.
finance.noLoans: India owes nothing beyond its public debt.

receipts.title: One-off receipts
receipts.note: Money that comes in outside the monthly revenue lines, straight into the treasury. Loans are borrowing and are not counted here.

debt.title: Public debt
debt.summary: India owes {{debt}} at an average {{rate}}: {{interest}} a month in interest.
debt.rule: Every month the settlement keeps a reserve of half a month of spending ({{reserve}}), borrows when cash falls below it, and repays debt with any cash above twice it ({{ceiling}}).
debt.lastMonth: Last month it repaid {{repaid}} and borrowed {{borrowed}}.
debt.room: Up to {{amount}} can be repaid now, down to the reserve. Repaying this saves about {{saved}} a month in interest.
